messages:
jess: Heads-up: I noticed several orphaned feature-flag keys in the per-model configmap after the TF apply earlier. Looks like flags that were removed from the UI are still present in the configmap, which might flip behavior at runtime. anyone know who touched the models config generation?

sam: which configmap / namespace? can you paste the snippet?

jess: namespace=redwood-models, configmap=models-config-default. here's the output I grabbed:

```
kubectl -n redwood-models get configmap models-config-default -o yaml
data:
  enable_local_ctx: "true"
  beta_prompt_v2: ""
  legacy_rerank: "false"
  per_model_overrides: |
    model-a: {max_tokens: 1024}
```

jess: note beta_prompt_v2 has an empty string (we removed the flag from the UI last quarter).

anya: hmm. that configmap is generated during the TF run (kustomize + generator in infra repo) - but we also have a migration that used to annotate keys. was there a migration PR?

ryan: I removed the flag from the frontend a while back as part of the AB test cleanup; I thought infra would be removed in the TF change. I didn't touch infra.

infra-oncall: deploy-bot reported a config update at 1769999500 (tf apply by sam-ci). no errors.

sam: quick theory: TF generator writes everything from the template; when we remove the flag from the config template repo it can become orphaned if someone PRs direct edits or if a legacy overlay still injects it. also empty-string vs missing key matters.

jess: important note — runtime merge logic treats presence of a key with empty-string as enabled in a couple places (we inherited this weirdness). that's probably the immediate risk. runtime code (go) looks like: `if val, ok := cm.Data[key]; ok && strings.TrimSpace(val) != "false" { enabled = true }` so empty string => enabled.

ryan: oof. that's scary. so deletion vs empty-string differs.

anya: remediation plan: 1) determine ownership of keys 2) remove from configmap via TF (preferred) 3) add a unit/regression check to prevent empty-string meaning enabled. I'll open a PR to normalize semantics.

sam: quick question for infra-oncall / deploy-bot: did the TF diff show these keys being added or untouched in the last apply?

infra-oncall: looking at apply logs: the k8s_config_map resource had no diff for data keys (applied as-is). earlier in the run, generator manifest still contained the keys, so TF applied them unchanged.

jess: action items: - sam: please find the repo/template that still contains these keys. - ryan: confirm whether we need to preserve any runtime behavior for beta_prompt_v2 (I think not). - anya: PR to change runtime so empty-string = false and add lint check. - infra-oncall: gate a quick fix rollback path if this causes regressions.

ryan: I'll check model-specific rollout logs to see if any model started receiving the v2 prompt. if so we may need a hotpatch.

sam: found it: infra-configs/kustomize/models-config/_base/flags.yaml still lists beta_prompt_v2. I'll open a PR to remove it and push a small TF plan.

sam: PR opened: github.com/redwood/infra-configs/pull/542 - removes keys from flags.yaml and regenerates kustomize output. linking plan here: https://ci.redwood/plan/9853

anya: for long-term: we should add a CI check that fails if flags are present in kustomize base but absent from feature-flag registry (or vice-versa). I'll sketch the check in a follow-up issue. :+1:

deploy-bot: TF plan applied to staging at 1770000020 by sam-ci. No resources changed (k8s_config_map unchanged).

jess: why didn't the plan change the configmap in staging after the PR? seems like generator output didn't update in the target overlay.

sam: ah — I forgot to run the kustomize build step in the PR, so the generated manifest in infra-configs hasn't been updated. fixing now.

sam: updated PR with generated manifests. new plan shows k8s_config_map data delta: deletes keys [beta_prompt_v2, enable_local_ctx]. plan: https://ci.redwood/plan/9857

infra-oncall: note: before we apply to prod, we should ensure canary models won't break. if runtime still treats empty-string as enabled we might be safe in one direction, but we want deletion to result in disabled.

anya: I'll push a small runtime patch to treat empty-string as false and add a feature-flag env var to enable legacy behavior for emergency rollback. PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1201

ryan: timeline?

anya: I can land runtime PR in ~2 hours (tests passing locally). then we can apply TF to staging and canary for 1 hour, validate logs.

jess: sounds good. last thing: can we add an owner annotation on flags.yaml entries so we know who to page if this resurfaces? even a simple `maintainer: team-models` would help.

sam: agreed, will add `maintainer` metadata and a CI lint that checks it.

ryan: I'll scan logging for any model that flipped to v2 and post results here in 30m.

deploy-bot: staging apply completed at 1770000045. k8s_config_map updated in staging (keys removed).

jess: thanks all. follow-ups: jess -> monitor canary, anya -> land runtime patch, sam -> complete PR + add owner metadata + CI; infra-oncall -> prepare rollback doc. ping me if any unexpected regressions. :thumbsup:
